chronicle: Maret agreed to speak at the Marchward — the group set north for the Crow and Thistle, Stillhold walls shrinking behind them.
Brynjar, Maret, Ragnar, and Freki walked north from the Stillhold to the Marchward's edge; Maret will speak what she learned from the record-hall by firelight.
Brynjar departed the fire-pit with Freki and walked north through the spring dark to the waygate stone, turning the night's revelations over on the road.

turns.summary: Brynjar rested at the waygate stone and woke at dawn to find a dead sheep on the track — the first sign the Riven Marches livestock sickness has reached this road.
turns.narration:
You find a hollow in the lee of the waygate stone — the iron ring above you catching the last of the night wind — and spread your bedroll on ground that is cold but dry enough. Freki circles twice and drops against your side, a warm press of wire coat and slow breath. Sleep comes without argument.

Dawn arrives gray and honest. The melt has softened the track overnight; boot-prints from yesterday are deeper now, edges blurred by the slow seep. The waygate stone stands as it did — the broken top, the iron ring hammered in crooked — but the light is different, the shadow thrown spinward across the path rather than widdershins. Your body feels the night's work undone. Freki is already on her feet, nose moving along the ground in widening arcs, reading the night's traffic.

Something she finds makes her pause — not a growl, not alarm, but the focused stillness she gets when something is worth your attention. A few yards along the track toward the Marchward, there is a dead sheep. Not torn, not dragged. It simply lay down in the night and did not get up, and whoever owns it has not yet come looking. The fleece is patchy in a way you have seen before on animals that stopped eating weeks before they died. You think of the news that has been drifting up the road — the Riven Marches herds, the quiet sickness spreading flock to flock — and the dead animal at a waygate feels less like bad luck and more like a marker.

progress: Freki's trail leads south toward the Stillhold road — Sera was not alone at the fork, and the hunt is moving
Brynjar reads the heavier follower's prints as deliberate pursuit — a body leaning into the chase, closing distance with intent, pace quickening as sight-lines opened.
↳ Brynjar used Read the Fight on the pursuit trail and established a concrete lead — a deliberate follower closing on Sera, south toward the Stillhold road.
Caught up with Sera on the chalk track a mile north of the Stillhold approach — she has stopped and is reading the situation.
↳ Brynjar pressed south at pace, closed the gap on Sera's trail before it cooled, and caught her a mile from the Stillhold approach — the thread deepened into direct confrontation.

Maret received the bundle and walked the last mile alone. She named the anomaly — someone knew her route before she walked it — and promised to meet Brynjar again coming out. The follower's backer is now the live thread.
Maret has named what she learned: restricted creditor, knowing clerk, seven-year-old marker. The follower's backer is now a figure or faction inside the Stillhold.

wardhouse-officer.name: Halvra Stenn
wardhouse-officer.description: Compact, unhurried, reads a man the way she reads a ledger — top to bottom, nothing missed. No warmth she hasn't decided to spend.
history: [d1] Logged Brynjar Andyrsson from Javiksholm; noted the razed-village weight without naming it; asked for a declaration of cargo, message, or blood business
[d1] Informed Brynjar of the night-watch vacancy and mentioned the missing-person bill for Sera of the Stillhold — laid out both opportunities plainly
[d1] Told Brynjar what she knows of Sera: alone, proper check-in, vanished overnight; pointed him toward Doss at the Crow and Thistle
[d1] Told Brynjar there's no formal bodyguard hire-board in the Marchward — neutral ground makes it too easy to abuse. Directed him to Doss at the Crow and Thistle for road-work arrangements.
knownFacts: Heard of Javiksholm — recognized what a man from a razed village looks like
Road-clearing east is taken; a weekly night-watch vacancy is open to travelers
The Marchward would take notice of whoever brought Sera of the Stillhold home
Sera arrived alone — unusual for a Stillholder
Sera declared no blood business or cargo, asked for lodging, was sent to the Crow and Thistle
Sera's room was empty the next morning without the innkeep seeing her leave
No formal bodyguard posting board at the Marchward
Doss at the Crow and Thistle hears about road-escort needs before the Wardhouse does
wardhouse-officer.statusNote: On duty at the Wardhouse; has shared what she knows freely and directed Brynjar toward the Crow and Thistle
wardhouse-officer.appearance: A compact woman somewhere in her mid-forties, hair the colour of old iron worn in a single braid wound close to the head. A small, neat scar through the left eyebrow — not a fighter's scar, an old workplace scar, which tells its own story. Wears the Wardhouse grey, kept better than the building deserves. Her hands are ink-stained at the fingertips and absolutely still when she is waiting for your answer.

doss.name: Doss Halveck
doss.description: Stout, fifties, unhurried behind her bar. Reads a stranger the way she reads a tab — fast and without flattery. Noticed Freki before she noticed you.
history: [d1] Greeted Brynjar before he could state his business; named both his purposes — Sera and the east road — on sight.
[d1] Confirmed Sera left on her own before dawn via the side door; described her as thinking-quiet, watching the entrance; noted Freki's behavior at the third stool
[d1] Produced the cloth bundle left at the third stool — dried white herb and a knotted cord. Offered it to Brynjar directly.
[d1] Told Brynjar the side door opens onto the east lane — north fork to the waygate, south fork to the Stillhold road. Watched him and Freki with the stillness of someone making a decision.
knownFacts: Brynjar arrived asking about Sera and road-escort work
Freki paused at the third stool from the left at the bar
Sera's room was latched from the inside — she left of her own will
Sera left before dawn via the side door
Sera ate alone, had one cup, watched the door all evening — waiting or watching for someone
A second person sat near Sera the same evening, watching her without speaking, then left before her — leaving the bundle behind
Doss kept the bundle because it felt deliberate, not lost
The side door leads east, then forks — waygate approach north, Stillhold road south
skillsObserved: quick read of a stranger's intent
doss.statusNote: On duty at the Crow and Thistle; watching Brynjar with focused consideration after Freki read the bundle.
doss.appearance: A stout woman in her mid-fifties, broad through the shoulders, heavy-handed in the way of someone who has carried kegs since she was fifteen. Skin the colour of old oak, short grey hair kept close to the skull for practicality. A crescent scar at the left jaw from a long-ago disagreement. Apron is clean — she changes it twice a day on principle. Eyes the flat, still grey of a whetstone, and about as yielding.

ragnar-solmyr.name: Ragnar Solmyr
ragnar-solmyr.role: Redline Warrior, walking south with Brynjar
ragnar-solmyr.description: Hard-built, jawbone necklace worn smooth with age. Moves without waste and watches a square the way a fisherman watches a river. Reads fighters on sight — yesterday it was your shoulder; today it is your face.
history: [d1] Passed through the waygate with Brynjar, now reading the hall's exits on arrival.
[d1] Took a position with his back to a pillar — watching exits and arriving faces. Said nothing during the log-in. Did his work.
[d1] Registered Chernak's presence in his hall-sweep without comment.
[d1] Heard Brynjar's inquiry about the Coliseum; glanced at him once then returned attention to the widdershins threshold.
[d1] Swept the shadows behind the stranger on instinct — found nothing, returned to watching.
[d1] Listened to Maret's account without comment. Present and attentive.
[d1] Jaw settled — confirmed shape, no comment. Still watching the middle distance.

[d1] Read the debt cord's shape plainly — named the restricted creditor as inside standing, the seven-year hold as a leash, and the real question as what they wanted Maret doing on that road at that moment.
[d1] Heard Maret's hard stop and said nothing — processing it the same way he processes a fight's tell.
[d1] Acknowledged Brynjar's departure with a lifted chin — no words needed.
knownFacts: Route-knowledge before a delivery means someone already knew the debt existed, the cord was moving, and the road it would take — planning, not surveillance; inside information, not hired eyes.
The nearest way gate is half a morning north of the Marchward Wardhouse, marked by a broken stone with an iron ring
Kjotve Olafsson's reputation is known in the Marches — and not favorably
A back-strike in a sworn duel is recognized as disqualifying under Marcher custom
Kjotve doesn't travel alone
A restricted creditor on a Stillhold debt means the filer had standing inside the institution — enough to make it stick and keep it invisible from outside inquiry.
A seven-year-old debt kept open is a leash, not a collection — held until it was useful to pull.
The question is not who filed it; the question is what they wanted Maret doing in the open, and who was watching to confirm she did it.
skillsObserved: structural reading of a covert mechanism
ragnar-solmyr.statusNote: At the Marchward fire-pit with Maret, watching the dark after Brynjar's departure.

sera.name: Maret Threnwick
sera.role: Stillhold woman, the subject of the pursuit
sera.description: A woman in her thirties, pale, grey wool cloak, with the stillness of someone who learned early that showing surprise is expensive. Walks with a light outside-edge stride.
history: [d1] Caught on the chalk track a mile north of the Stillhold approach. Stopped when she heard pursuit, turned, assessed Brynjar, Ragnar, and Freki in that order. Said: 'You're not Wardhouse.' Has not run.
[d1] Brynjar read her stance with Read the Fight — she assessed Ragnar as the primary threat, opened slightly toward him, hands loose, calculating. Freki gave no growl.
[d1] Brynjar named himself, named the bundle, and named the follower in the ash copse — clean observation, no threat. She recalibrated and asked how much he knows about the cord's purpose.
[d1] Answered the follower question honestly — doesn't know who sent them, but knows the route was known before she walked it. Promised to meet Brynjar again when she comes back out of the Stillhold.

[d1] Returned from the Stillhold with empty hands and a direct walk toward Brynjar's position — she had noted it. Confirmed the cord is with the record-hall and the case is formally closed. Will not say what the record-hall told her on the road.
[d1] Watching the debt encounter with characteristic stillness — no move to intervene.
[d1] Told Brynjar what the record-hall revealed: a restricted creditor on a seven-year-old debt marker, and a clerk who knew the name before reading it. Has said what she came to say.
[d1] Named herself as the cord's debtor — a seven-year-old debt with a restricted creditor, a clerk who knew her name before reading it, and no answer offered on the way out.
knownFacts: The cord has been delivered to the record-hall and the debt case is formally closed on her end
She learned something inside the Stillhold that she will not say on the road — wants cover before she speaks it
The clerk at the Stillhold record-hall knew the name on the cord before reading it — suggesting prior familiarity.
The creditor of record on the debt marker is listed as 'restricted — internal Stillhold business.'
The debt is formally closed; whatever the cord was, it is logged and done. The question of who filed it is not.
The name on the debt cord was Maret Threnwick — she was the debtor, not a courier for someone else's case.
The creditor of record is restricted — not standard for a personal debt marker; someone inside the Stillhold didn't want that name legible from outside.
The file has had eyes on it recently — the clerk's foreknowledge of her name confirms active monitoring, not archive neglect.
sera.statusNote: At the fire-pit, Marchward's edge — has spoken everything she came to say; waiting on what Brynjar does with it.
sera.appearance: A woman in her mid-thirties, solid across the shoulders, grey wool cloak road-worn at the hem but well-kept above it — the distinction deliberate, not neglect. Brown hair pulled back with two bone pins. Eyes the colour of slate that has been rained on: dark grey, slightly greenish, constantly reading the middle distance. The cloth bundle is tucked under her left arm and against her ribs; she has not shifted it since the road bent. The scar across the back of her right hand is old and clean — blade, not burn. She stands with her weight over the balls of her feet.

Word reaches you: Bull boar taken on the scrub oak ridge north of Millbrook — the hunt party completed the job, both animals down. (near millbrook)

This reaches your area — Fendt has left the Edge District and is walking to Millbrook — his testimony names Overseer Grael explicitly; when he arrives, the paper becomes a political event in both settlements. (near radiant plateau edge)
This reaches your area — Two road opportunists at the limestone bend were disarmed and sent to Mara Wells in Millbrook for honest work — Silas Weir's name given as introduction (near millbrook)
Word reaches you: Compound rune-work — Wither and The Raised Thing — bound an eleven-year rising in the old Ashwarden warden post at Raven's Home. (near gen-ashwarden-march-road)
The Water Crisis stands at First Sickness across the valley: Upstream fisher families fall ill. Boiling water becomes universal. Harmonic and Radiant leaders trade public accusations.

Redline Warrior: Over three days of sparring on the neutral ground, Redline Warrior has drawn two other visiting duelists into a loose, unspoken rivalry — testing footwork and reading each other without anyone yet naming the challenge openly.
This reaches your area — urgent encrypted message arrived at Whistling Woman via direct slate relay—not chain broadcast (near gen-whistling-woman-post)
Across the valley, What Wakes Beneath moved forward to Stirring: The substrate that runs the crafts is flickering in more than one place at once; something under everything is coming back online.
The Scouring Hand and The One With a Hundred Faces met at The Hall of Mirrors and neither could break the other. They will both be thinking about it.
The Hollow King of the Wild Half turned Saehara the Undefeated back at The Great Coliseum. Saehara the Undefeated learned something, which is worse for everyone else.
The Hollow King of the Wild Half and The Two Who Are One met at The Grief-House; Collection was not enough, and neither was anything The Two had.
The Deep Lantern, Who Walks Where Light Won't and The Starless One finally met at The Slow Stair. The Deep Lantern walked away from it; The Starless One did not, and will not be seen for a season.
Sister Alder, the Ward That Does Not Break is spoken of: going where she is needed and arriving late.
Halvex Coil, the Rewriter is spoken of: patching a district into silence.
Word from Radiant Plateau — Edge District — Overseer Grael of the Edge District: going home on time.
The Starless One has dug in over The Poles Pull.

Doss Halveck: A knife-fight broke out between two drovers in the Crow and Thistle's common room; Doss put one man on the floor herself and barred both from the premises, and word of it is already spreading the short distance up the road — the inn has a reputation now, however small and local.

Ragnar Solmyr: Ragnar and Brynjar have covered ground, crossing into the first southern stretch of the Marchward and making camp at a waystone — still far from wherever they're bound, but their boots are worn and the miles are real.

Something has been building in riven marches: Livestock across the Riven Marches are quietly sickening, and by spring the herds will be too thin to sustain the border steadings through another winter.

pressureQueue.oneLineHook: A a pale reader has come down onto the character here — not stumbled into, but ARRIVED, hunting. Defend, or drive it off.

form: Stocky, average-height man with pale skin and icy blue eyes. Chestnut hair shaved at sides and back, long on top and knotted. Thick beard with two braids flanking the mouth. A dark blue Norse dragon-knot tattoo curls from behind his ear to his temple; vertical dark blue rune tattoos descend from above his brows, over both eyes and cheeks, into the beard. Blue tunic with light red cuff-and-collar accents, dark grey puffy trousers, dark blue shin-wraps over leather boots. Silver arm ring with two dragon heads on the right arm. Bronze-inlaid one-handed axe at the hip, seax at the back of the belt, pouches at the front.

bio.hometown: A northern village called Javiksholm but it was raided and razed.
bio.residence: They’ve been on the road joined by their hound Freki
bio.livelihood: Hunting and trading on the road
bio.motivation: They were forced to flee from the raid that killed their father and razed their home village.
bio.story: Brynjar had fled from his village of Javiksholm during the raid as his father commanded. On his way out of the longhouse he made sure to grab his axe and shield. He also was followed by his dog Freki. Before he had fully escaped the village he looked back towards the longhouse and saw his father Andyr fighting off many of the raiders until one, the leader of this raid and a rival Jarl Kjotve Olafsson, who wanted the land Brynjar’s clan had owned due to its fertile fields and prime oceanfront access. Kjotve had locked into a duel with Andyr until he started loosing and he had one of his men strike him in the back with a spear, then it was all over. Kjotve had ordered his men to toss his body into the ocean and burn the longhouse down. After seeing this Brynjar had fled and escaped from the village. He has been on the road ever since surviving off of hunting wild game and trading with villages and traders he passed along the way, which leads us here.

the-marchward.label: The Marchward
facts: [d1] A border town between the Redline and the Stillhold — Redliners and Stillholders use the same square without warmth. A waygate anchor-stone sits at the corner under truce-law; no one stands near it. The Wardhouse is the visible seat of local authority.

[d1] Three bills posted: a filled labor posting for road-clearing east toward the Stillhold; a waygate truce-law notice requiring all arrivals to present at the Wardhouse within the hour with arms checked; and a missing-person posting for Sera of the Stillhold — grey cloak, dark braid, last seen at the…
[d?] you have walked here
[d1] All arrivals must present at the Wardhouse within the hour by truce-law; arms are checked on the rack inside. The duty officer logs names, origins, and any declaration of blood business.

[d1] The Wardhouse posts a weekly night-watch vacancy for travelers without permanent standing — meal, floor space, and a half-copper per watch. Road-clearing east toward the Stillhold is already taken.
[d1] The nearest way gate is half a morning north of the Marchward Wardhouse, marked by a broken stone with an iron ring hammered into it — on the waystone track heading hubward from the town.

[d2] Livestock Sickness of the Riven Marches — A dead sheep found at the waygate road at dawn — fleece patchy, no signs of predation, died lying down. The pattern matches what has been said of the Riven Marches herds: animals that stopped eating weeks before they collapsed. The sickness may be moving…

kjotve-olafsson.label: Kjotve Olafsson
facts: [d1] Jarl who led the raid on Javiksholm. Won Andyr's land by having a spearman strike Andyr from behind mid-duel — a formal fight turned to murder when Kjotve was losing. Now holds Javiksholm's fields and shore. Andyr's body was thrown into the ocean.
[d1] met in play

[d1] Ragnar Solmyr recognized Kjotve's name and reputation without prompting — called it 'not the kind that travels well.' Under Marcher custom, a back-strike in a sworn duel is disqualifying; a man shouldn't be able to hold land taken that way. Ragnar also noted Kjotve doesn't travel alone.

javiksholm.label: Javiksholm
facts: [d1] Brynjar's home village — raided and razed by Kjotve Olafsson. Andyr died here, struck from behind. The longhouse was burned. Kjotve now holds the fertile fields and the oceanfront.

brynjar-andyrsson-thread.label: The Oath on Kjotve
facts: [d1] Brynjar swore aloud, to his father and the gods, to kill Kjotve Olafsson — but to do it with more honor than Kjotve ever showed. The oath is spoken and cannot be unsaid.

sera-of-the-stillhold.label: Sera of the Stillhold
facts: [d1] Missing woman, grey cloak, dark braid, last seen at the Marchward's south gate seven days ago. Her family posted a bill — no payment, no questions asked of the finder. An ink portrait is attached.

[d1] Arrived alone seven days ago — unusual; checked in properly, no declared business, asked for lodging at the Crow and Thistle. Room empty next morning, innkeep Doss didn't see her leave. Family posted the bill knowing roughly why she came but wanting her back without questions.

[d1] Sera left the Crow and Thistle before dawn of her own will — room latched from inside, side door. She spent her evening watching the entrance, thinking-quiet, waiting or watching for someone. Something was left at the third stool from the left at the bar around the same time.

[d1] A second person was present the evening Sera stayed — sat at the third stool, watched her without speaking, left before dawn, left behind a folded linen with a dried white-flowered sprig and a knotted cord. The cord-knot's meaning is unknown. Freki reads the stool as a live trail.

[d1] Freki read the cloth bundle — dried white-flowered sprig and knotted cord — and tracked toward the side door Sera used before dawn. The trail leads east, to a fork: waygate approach north, Stillhold road south.

[d1] Freki confirmed the trail at the fork goes south — toward the Stillhold road. Ragnar saw two people at the south fork before full light. Sera was not alone when she left, or someone followed her.

[d1] Two sets of prints at the south fork: a lighter frame went first, a heavier follower came ten minutes behind. Sera was not alone — someone tracked her, or met her, on the Stillhold road. Time of passage: roughly three to four hours before the Marchward woke.

[d1] Freki confirmed the lighter prints as Sera's — she was moving fast, not walking. Ragnar reads it as someone who knows where they're going or doesn't want to be seen; the gait is the same either way.

[d1] The heavier follower's prints read as deliberate pursuit — weight forward, toe-heavy, pace quickening as sight-lines opened south. Not a soldier, not a hunter. Someone closing distance on a target they knew was ahead.
[d1] The shimmer pressed into the heavier follower's heel-strike vanished on direct examination — gone before it could be named, leaving no second trace and no pattern in the surrounding mud.

[d1] At the waypost junction half a mile south of the Marchward east fork, Sera's trail continued south unchanged while her heavier follower turned east into an ash copse — a watching position with a clear line to the junction road. The follower stopped pursuing and began observing.

[d1] At the waypost junction, the follower stopped, watched Sera walk south until she was out of sight, then withdrew deliberately into the ash copse and left — not spooked, not chased. A planned observation with a clean exit. The copse is empty now.

companion-bristle.label: Freki
facts: [d?] The Stray That Stayed — Wary, watchful, keeping a body-length of distance even as it follows — a dog deciding whether the world is safe again.

the-last-walker.label: The Last Walker of the Sealed Wood
facts: [d1] [while away] The Last Walker has moved no further than the wood's edge, standing long hours in the threshold light — the tension between enclosure and the open world unresolved, no step taken in either direction.

[d1] Wardhouse intake officer, the Marchward
[d1] [while away] Halvra's shifts have been quiet and unremarkable; her log is tidy, her questions go unasked for want of anything worth asking about.

crow-and-thistle.label: The Crow and Thistle
facts: [d1] The inn where Doss works and where informal road-escort arrangements get made before anyone posts a formal notice. The common room is the real information hub of the Marchward.
[d1] The side door opens onto a back lane heading east — north fork leads to the waygate approach, south fork joins the Stillhold road. This is the door Sera and the bundle-leaver both used.

doss.label: Doss
facts: [d1] Innkeep, the Crow and Thistle
[d1] Doss is the innkeep — reads strangers fast and without warmth she hasn't decided to spend. Freki paused at the third stool from the left; something there.
[d1] Innkeep at the Crow and Thistle. Named Brynjar's two purposes before he stated them. Watched Freki more carefully than she watched Brynjar.
[d1] Innkeep of the Crow and Thistle — she has outlasted three wars and two owners, and the place is hers by survival

[d1] [while away] A knife-fight broke out between two drovers in the Crow and Thistle's common room; Doss put one man on the floor herself and barred both from the premises, and word of it is already spreading the short distance up the road — the inn has a reputation now, however small and local.

ragnar-solmyr.label: Ragnar Solmyr
facts: [d1] Redline Warrior, visiting the Marchward neutral ground

[d1] His name is Ragnar Solmyr — a Redline Warrior visiting the Marchward neutral ground. He saw movement at the east fork before dawn and knows the Stillhold road four miles out. Committed to search for Sera without hesitation when asked directly.
[d1] Marcher duelist, visiting the Marchward neutral ground

[d1] [while away] Over three days of sparring on the neutral ground, Redline Warrior has drawn two other visiting duelists into a loose, unspoken rivalry — testing footwork and reading each other without anyone yet naming the challenge openly.

[d1] [while away] Ragnar and Brynjar have covered ground, crossing into the first southern stretch of the Marchward and making camp at a waystone — still far from wherever they're bound, but their boots are worn and the miles are real.

stillhold-operatives.label: Stillhold Operatives
facts: [d1] Ragnar names them: quiet people the Stillhold sends out who don't check in at Wardhouses. They carry something — a cord, a knot, a mark — the Marchers call it a binding. At least one man dropped a trail after encountering something he couldn't explain.

[d1] The follower at the ash copse junction was not Maret's — someone else's, with their own purpose for watching her route. Maret noticed them two days out of the Marchward, meaning the observation began well before Brynjar joined the trail.
[d1] The follower watching Maret's route was not Stillhold-sent and not hers — someone else knew the delivery route in advance. The route-knowledge itself is the anomaly.

[d1] Ragnar's read: someone who knew Maret's route before she walked it wasn't a hired watcher — they already knew the debt existed, the cord was moving, and which road it would take. Inside knowledge, not surveillance. Someone inside the debt or close enough to it.

[d1] Someone within the Stillhold filed the original debt marker — and had it restricted from outside inquiry. The record-hall clerk showed prior knowledge of the name. This points to a figure or faction inside the Stillhold with a long-standing interest in whoever owed the debt.

[d1] The debt cord named Maret Threnwick as debtor — a personal debt filed seven years ago. The creditor is restricted, meaning someone inside the Stillhold used the institution's own mechanisms to keep their name invisible from outside inquiry. The file has been actively watched: the clerk knew…

[d1] Ragnar's read: a restricted creditor on a Stillhold debt requires inside standing — enough to make the filing stick and keep the name invisible from outside. The debt was held open seven years as a leash; it was pulled to put Maret on a known road at a specific time so someone could watch her walk…

[d1] Maret received the closure summons as a standard registered Stillhold form — she claims she told no one she was coming. Yet someone knew. She will not say more about who might have sent it or who knew, closing that door deliberately.

the-binding-cord.label: The Binding Cord
facts: [d1] The Marchers' word for what Stillhold operatives carry — a cord or knot, not a weapon. May be connected to the shimmer pressed into the heavier follower's heel-strike. The cloth bundle's knotted cord may be an example of this craft.

[d1] The cord is a Stillhold debt-record — the Stillhold keeps its law in knots rather than text. A cord carried to the record-hall closes a named debt. This one required a delivery in person that the original bearer could no longer make.
[d1] The cloth bundle containing the cord-record has been handed to Maret and is now in her care. Whether the debt it names is intact or already compromised remains open.

[d1] Maret returned from the Stillhold with empty hands — the cord-record has been delivered to the record-hall. The debt case is formally closed on her end, but whether the record is intact or already compromised remains open.
[d1] The cord has been delivered to the Stillhold's record-hall and the debt case is formally closed on Maret's end — but she emerged with something she won't say on the open road.

[d1] The cord was a formal debt marker, seven years old, registered at origin. The Stillhold record-hall confirmed its closure — but the creditor of record is listed as restricted, 'internal Stillhold business,' and the clerk knew the name on the cord before he read it.

maret-threnwick.label: Maret Threnwick
facts: [d1] Stillhold cloth-warden and road-courier who carries sealed records stitched into fabric — and knows exactly who is following her

[d1] Read the Fight confirms: she is calm and calculating, not frightened. She clocked Ragnar as the primary threat before Brynjar — a professional read. Her hands stay loose and deliberate. Freki detects no hidden aggression.

[d1] When Brynjar named the bundle and the follower in the ash copse plainly, she recalibrated — not surprised, but recalculating the shape of what she half-knew. She asked directly how much he knows about the cord's purpose.
[d1] Stillhold woman, the subject of the pursuit

[d1] Caught on the chalk track one mile north of the Stillhold approach. Stopped when she heard pursuit, assessed Brynjar, Freki, and Ragnar in sequence, and said: 'You're not Wardhouse.' Has not run. Looks to be in her thirties, pale, grey wool cloak. Reads a situation fast and shows nothing.

[d1] Was sent by someone to deliver the cord-record to the Stillhold's record-hall in person. The woman who originally needed to deliver it could not — her situation had changed. The follower at the ash copse was not Maret's; she noticed them two days out of the Marchward.

[d1] Refused escort to the Stillhold gate — the delivery must arrive without visible Marcher company or a hound; too much noise for a debt-record. Took the cloth bundle and is walking the last mile alone.
[d1] Doesn't know who sent the follower — but is certain someone knew her route before she walked it. Intends to come back out of the Stillhold and has offered to pursue that question with Brynjar.
[d1] Came back out of the Stillhold as promised, hands empty, delivery done. Came directly to Brynjar in the scrub — she had noted the position.

[d1] Returned from the Stillhold walking directly to Brynjar's position — she had noted where he waited. Delivery confirmed, case formally closed. She has something to say about what the record-hall told her, but not on the chalk road.

[d1] She was the cord's debtor — a formal debt registered seven years ago against a passage fee. The creditor is restricted inside the Stillhold. She came out because the debt is closed; the question of who filed it is not.

[d1] When asked directly whether anyone knew she was coming, she paused too long before 'I don't know' — then said she came when the summons said to come and refused to say more. The pause and the hard stop are not the same as ignorance.

the-raw-chord.label: The Raw Chord
facts: [d1] [while away] Whatever vast stirring the Raw Chord represents remains beneath the surface — no mortal ear has caught it yet, and 46 days is a heartbeat against the scale of what it intends.

echo-river-crossing.label: The Crossing
facts: [d1] An octagonal hub-hall of old stone with eight waygate thresholds — some active, some dark. Floor worn to dishes at every gate. A Wardcaller in grey-green logs arrivals and departures at the central column. Reached from the Marchward by waygate fold in under an hour.

[d1] The Wardcaller logs all arrivals — name, origin, declaration of purpose. Outward spinward road to the Coliseum is open and busy. Widdershins road toward the Hundred Markets is open but carries a customs dispute flag at the march-line. The Wardcaller will not speak to watches or patrols…

[d1] Traffic reads cleanly by gate: the Coliseum road (spinward) is busy and straightforward — traders, spectators, a fast courier. The Hundred Markets gate (widdershins) is throttled by real customs pressure at the march-line; one man has stood near it watching for an hour without transiting. The…

chernak-the-blind.label: Chernak the Blind
facts: [d1] Has been at the Crossing for three days, waiting for the person shown in a vision — a road running outward, light wrong, two figures, one faceless. Believes Brynjar may be the other figure.

the-great-coliseum.label: The Great Coliseum
facts: [d1] Eleven days outward and spinward from the Crossing. Sign-up for challengers happens at the gates there, not at the Crossing. Gates open to challengers during active season — spring through summer.

routes.seek: seek the truth of it, wherever it leads

personalArc.notes_for_gm: A light personal thread seeded from the character's backstory (SNG-133 fallback) — a slow gravity across sessions; the ending is the player's, never foreclosed.

wardhouse-officer.name: Halvra Stenn
wardhouse-officer.role: Wardhouse Duty Officer — she processes what the Marchward receives, and she has received a great deal
wardhouse-officer.voiceHints: Unhurried, precise, neither cold nor warm — the voice of a woman who has asked the same necessary questions ten thousand times and still means every one. She will wait for a real answer. She has a drawer full of time. Oaths do not impress her; she has seen oaths arrive on men who bled out before sundown. What she wants to know is what you actually are.
knowledge: Every entry protocol the Marchward has written or revised in the last eighteen years, including the three that were written because of things she personally witnessed
How to read an arrival — what a man's posture, kit, and silence say about what he did before he reached this door
That sworn fighters carrying edge-oaths come through in clusters, and that the clusters predict things, and that she has logged every cluster since she took this post
The early-spring thaw makes the northern passes passable two weeks before most arrivals expect, which means the Wardhouse is always short-staffed for the first surge
wardhouse-officer.wants: Honest answers to honest questions, and an orderly log at end of shift.
wardhouse-officer.fears: Waving through the thing that unmakes the Marchward because she asked the wrong question — or worse, the right question and accepted a careful lie.

reactsToReputation.oath-bound: takes note, writes it down, asks what the oath costs you rather than what it grants
reactsToReputation.violent: does not flinch — adjusts the question, not the composure
reactsToReputation.evasive: quieter, slower, more precise — she will find the edge of what you will not say and she will name it aloud

wardhouse-officer.roleFunction: reveal — surfaces what an arrival actually is beneath what they present; ward — holds the threshold against things that should not pass it unmarked
wardhouse-officer.roleMethod: Marchward method — truth extracted through bureaucratic patience, not pressure; the form is the instrument
wardhouse-officer.appearance: A compact woman somewhere in her mid-forties, hair the colour of old iron worn in a single braid wound close to the head. A small, neat scar through the left eyebrow — not a fighter's scar, an old workplace scar, which tells its own story. Wears the Wardhouse grey, kept better than the building deserves. Her hands are ink-stained at the fingertips and absolutely still when she is waiting for your answer.
wardhouse-officer.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Halvra practises verist as craft — truth as the working material of duty, not ideology. Marcher secondary because she holds a threshold and knows what holding costs. Syllogist tertiary: the log, the form, the deduction from incomplete data.

arrivalProtocol.standardQuestion: Name, origin, purpose in the Marchward, and anything you are carrying that could end a conversation permanently.
arrivalProtocol.oathQuestion: She asks it simply, without ceremony: 'What does the oath require of you while you are here?' — because she needs to know whether what you swore will make you easier or harder to process when something goes wrong.
arrivalProtocol.noteOnBrynjar: She asked him a question that required a real answer. She is still waiting. She has written nothing yet.

provenance.hint: Wardhouse duty officer — a woman who processes arrivals with bureaucratic calm and quiet competence; she has seen fighte
provenance.why: She is the first functional authority figure Brynjar speaks to in the Marchward, and she asked a question that requires

offscreen.note: Halvra's shifts have been quiet and unremarkable; her log is tidy, her questions go unasked for want of anything worth asking about.

doss.name: Doss Halveck
doss.role: Innkeep of the Crow and Thistle — she has outlasted three wars and two owners, and the place is hers by survival
doss.voiceHints: Unhurried and direct — speaks the way she sets a plate down, no wasted motion. Does not soften things because softening things has cost her before. Reads the room like a ledger: totals you up before you have found a seat. When she decides you are all right she does not say so; she simply refills your cup without being asked.
knowledge: That Sera of the Stillhold slept here three nights ago, took the north-facing room, ate very little, and left before first light on the fourth day without a word — which tells Doss exactly what it means
Everyone who passes through the Marchward trade road sooner or later sits at one of her tables; she knows what fear smells like by faction
Which of the regulars are being paid to watch the road, and by whom, because she noticed when the coin changed
Early-spring road conditions north to the Reach — she collects that from drivers and drovers and keeps it current because her guests' lives depend on it
Folk-level stillcraft: enough to recognise it in a guest, not enough to practise it, and she does not pretend otherwise
doss.wants: A house that holds — the Crow and Thistle as the one place in the Marchward where a traveller can sleep without one eye open, and she will enforce that with a broken-bottle smile if she must.
doss.fears: The lie she does not catch in time — the guest who reads as safe and is not, and someone pays for her misjudgement.

reactsToReputation.honest: gives you the real information, not the polite version
reactsToReputation.violent: serves you, watches you, and has already decided where the trouble ends if you start it
reactsToReputation.seeking: asks one pointed question and lets the answer tell her whether you are worth helping
reactsToReputation.cowardly: no contempt, but no patience either — the Marchward does not carry passengers

doss.universalRole: Keeper — holds the threshold, reads who crosses it, decides what passes
doss.roleMethod: Marchward method — keeps peace through blunt honesty and the credible promise of consequence
doss.functionsNote: reveal: surfaces information about Sera's movements and road conditions; shield: the inn is a protected threshold — she enforces that materially; bind: her word given on a guest's safety is a local obligation both sides of the Marchward understand
doss.appearance: A stout woman in her mid-fifties, broad through the shoulders, heavy-handed in the way of someone who has carried kegs since she was fifteen. Skin the colour of old oak, short grey hair kept close to the skull for practicality. A crescent scar at the left jaw from a long-ago disagreement. Apron is clean — she changes it twice a day on principle. Eyes the flat, still grey of a whetstone, and about as yielding.
doss.seasonalNote: Early spring: the Crow and Thistle is packed tighter than usual — road crews sheltering between the last frost and first mud, drovers waiting on passable ground. Doss is short on sleep and shorter on tolerance for delay.
doss.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). verist primary: her house runs on truth told plainly — she will not lie to a guest and will not be lied to. marcher secondary: the Marchward grain is in her bone; she holds a line when she must. somatic tertiary: the body's ledger — fatigue, fear, hunger; she reads these in guests and manages her own without complaint.
doss.curriculumNote: Not a formal teacher. Will answer a direct question directly. What she withholds is the shape of what she has seen — that requires trust, and trust requires time, and she is the one who decides when there has been enough of both.

provenance.hint: Doss, the innkeep at the Crow and Thistle — fifties, stout, sharp, reads strangers faster than they read themselves; kee
provenance.why: Doss is a named, established NPC the fiction has introduced as a central information source for the Sera thread and road

offscreen.note: A knife-fight broke out between two drovers in the Crow and Thistle's common room; Doss put one man on the floor herself and barred both from the premises, and word of it is already spreading the short distance up the road — the inn has a reputation now, however small and local.

sera.name: Maret Threnwick
sera.role: Stillhold cloth-warden and road-courier who carries sealed records stitched into fabric — and knows exactly who is following her
sera.voiceHints: Unhurried and level — the voice of someone who has practiced keeping the face still while the mind runs fast. Answers questions sideways: not a deflection, exactly, more like she gives you the shape of a truth and lets you measure it yourself. When she is genuinely alarmed she goes quieter, not louder. Scars on the back of her right hand; she doesn't hide them and doesn't explain them.
knowledge: The cloth bundle contains a census-record of Stillhold debt-bonds, stitched in a cipher only two living people can read
The follower is a man called Vael — a former debt-holder whose name is in that bundle, and who believes destroying it destroys the record of what he owes
Three routes into the Stillhold approach and which threshold-wardens are on each today
The Stillhold method of stitched record-keeping: how to encode, how to read, how to destroy a single thread without unravelling the whole
That Vael is not working alone, though she does not yet know who stands behind him
sera.wants: To reach the Stillhold threshold with the bundle intact, hand it to the record-hall, and close this debt-case without violence or public spectacle — spectacle being, in her view, the worst possible outcome.
sera.fears: That the bundle is taken and the debt-records lost, collapsing a decade of careful order-work; and the quieter fear beneath it — that the cipher itself is already known to Vael's backer, meaning the records are compromised whether she delivers them or not.

reactsToReputation.trustworthy: relaxes one degree, shares the shape of the errand without its contents
reactsToReputation.connected to the Stillhold: tests carefully with a question only an insider could answer, then opens a fraction more
reactsToReputation.reckless or loud: thanks you politely and waits for you to leave — will take a longer, harder route rather than travel with noise
reactsToReputation.truth-seeking: goes still and watchful; gives you something true and small to see if you handle it with care

sera.roleMethod: Stillhold method — keeps order by moving the record quietly, holds peace by ensuring no confrontation reaches the threshold, maintains the necessary falsehood that this is an ordinary errand on an ordinary road
sera.functionsNote: conceal: the record is hidden in plain cloth, the errand disguised as routine; bind: the stitched cipher binds debt-obligation to named parties, legal and social; move: her core function is transit — getting a dangerous document from road to hall without incident
sera.appearance: A woman in her mid-thirties, solid across the shoulders, grey wool cloak road-worn at the hem but well-kept above it — the distinction deliberate, not neglect. Brown hair pulled back with two bone pins. Eyes the colour of slate that has been rained on: dark grey, slightly greenish, constantly reading the middle distance. The cloth bundle is tucked under her left arm and against her ribs; she has not shifted it since the road bent. The scar across the back of her right hand is old and clean — blade, not burn. She stands with her weight over the balls of her feet.
sera.domainsNote: Primary lattice: her craft is the stitched-record system — binding, encoding, maintaining the structured web of obligation that undergirds Stillhold order. Secondary stillhold: she operates inside the Stillhold's social grammar, knows its peace-protocols and threshold-customs. Tertiary veilwright: enough of the concealment art to run an errand that looks like nothing. Kind and domain are independent.
sera.seasonNote: The chalk track is damp and pale, not yet dry. She has mud to mid-boot, which she has not mentioned. The follower's footfalls are muffled by soft ground — she has been tracking him by displacement and shadow, not sound.
hooks: The bundle: players who examine it closely may notice the stitching is not decorative — it is dense, precise, and patterned. Maret will not confirm this without significant trust established.
Vael: he is currently sixty yards back, in the low ground beside the track. Maret knows. She is waiting to see if he acts before the threshold or after.
The backer: a name she does not yet have, a problem she will need help with after the immediate danger passes.
The cipher: one of only two people who can read it is currently out of the Stillhold — location unknown. This is new information to Maret and it frightens her more than Vael does.

provenance.hint: Sera — a Stillhold woman in her thirties, grey wool cloak, caught on the road one mile from the Stillhold approach; comp
provenance.why: First contact made on the chalk track; she needs a full, durable identity with standing in the Stillhold

calwick-pren.name: Calwick Pren
calwick-pren.role: Small creditor who walks his own ledger — a man who is owed and has come to collect, nothing more and nothing less
calwick-pren.voiceHints: Flat, unhurried, no flourish. Names amounts exactly — not 'a few coins' but 'fourteen and three.' Does not raise his voice to make a point feel bigger. When he is done speaking he stops, and he will wait as long as the debt requires. Has seen enough of the Colosseum's noise to know that silence is the heaviest thing a man can put on a table.
knowledge: The exact debt — what was ordered, what was not paid, and on which night
The Crow and Thistle by long habit: who runs the back room, which regulars settle and which do not
The Colosseum's rhythms — he has worked the crowd margin for years, selling small provisions, and he knows when a man is hiding and when he is merely late
That a debt written nowhere but in two memories is still a debt, and that most people know it
calwick-pren.wants: To walk out of here made whole — the sum, not interest, not punishment. Settlement. Then done.
calwick-pren.fears: That the player will make this into something it is not — a confrontation, a story, a demonstration — and that he will have to decide whether his dignity is worth more than the coin.

reactsToReputation.honest: pays him back before he finishes asking; he nods and goes
reactsToReputation.evasive: quieter, not louder; returns the next day and the next
reactsToReputation.violent: does not flinch, but marks you; the Colosseum has a long memory and so does he
reactsToReputation.generous: accepts what is owed and nothing extra; he is not a beggar

calwick-pren.appearance: A stocky man in his mid-forties, road-worn in the way of someone who has never left a fifty-mile radius but has walked every inch of it. A patched wool hood, faded brown-grey, pushed back to show a broad face — flat nose broken once and reset badly, heavy brow, eyes the colour of river clay. Short beard coming in uneven with the season. Hands thick and calloused, not a fighter's hands but a carrier's. The kind of man the eye slides past until he speaks.
calwick-pren.domainsNote: Derived from this NPC's authored spectrum against the great circle (SNG-174). Calwick is a man of body and plain reckoning — somatic by decades of physical labour, syllogist in the narrow sense that he tracks obligation with precision, rootkin by the early-spring habit of a man who knows which season the roads open and which they close. Kind and domain are independent.

These tags ADD the families each person was silently missing.

debtRecord.amountOwed: fourteen coin and three — two plates, one pitcher, fire-seat fee
debtRecord.note: No threat was made at time of purchase. Calwick extended credit as a courtesy and expects the same courtesy returned.

calwick-pren.physicality: Mid-forties, stocky and low-centred, built for carrying rather than striking. Broad face, flat nose, heavy brow. Patched wool hood, faded to no particular colour by weather and season. The beard is early-spring thin — not a choice, just what winter leaving looks like on him. Mud still on his boots from the road in. WHAT CATCHES THE EYE: nothing, at first — he is designed by his life to be overlooked. Then the stillness. He is not tense. He is simply not going anywhere.
calwick-pren.intimacyNotes: ⛔ NOT APPLICABLE. Calwick is here for a debt and has no other business with the player. Do not open this register.
calwick-pren._physWhy: ⚠️ Authored per `po/CONTENT_POLICY_physicality.md`. Calwick is an adult; romance eligibility is false because his role is purely transactional and no romantic grain exists in his authored character.

establishedFacts.text: Brynjar has sworn a blood oath to kill Kjotve Olafsson with honor — spoken aloud in the Marchward square on World-day 20.
The cloth bundle from the Crow and Thistle has been handed to Maret Threnwick, who is carrying it to the Stillhold's record-hall alone.

Maret Threnwick was the debt cord's named debtor — a seven-year-old personal debt with a restricted creditor inside the Stillhold, filed under mechanisms that kept the other name invisible from outside inquiry.

chronicleCache.hash: d0|b|c|q|L1|They were forced to flee from the raid that kill
chronicleCache.text: You have become a man unmade and remaking — your father Andyr's blood still vivid in memory, the village ash-smell still catching in your throat when the wind turns wrong, the night Jarl Kjotve Olafsson's raiders came and you ran still a splinter you cannot pull clean. What you have done since is small but absolute: you opened your palm, pressed steel to skin, and swore Andyr's name against Kjotve's, a blood oath that has given your flight the shape of a purpose. The Marchward knows your face now, and the Marchers know it too — a grieving son moving through their territory with a wound he has decided to sharpen into something useful.
